facts.value: The GDPx score averages each model across all 11 domains, each weighted equally, as is each partner within a domain.
facts.where: GDPx Leaderboard section (page text)
facts.quote: The GDPx score averages each model across all 11 domains, each weighted equally, as is each partner within a domain.

facts.value: The default score uses the intended grading method for each task and takes the average across 3 attempts.
facts.where: GDPx Leaderboard section (page text)
facts.quote: Tasks use a combination of binary and continuous grading depending on the domain. The default score uses the intended grading method for each task and takes the average across 3 attempts.

facts.where: newsletter, methodology
facts.quote: For the headline score, we report pass@1 across three attempts.

facts.where: newsletter, methodology
facts.quote: The default time limit for a GDPx task is 8 hours, though some tasks had shorter time limits.
facts.note: whole-system measurement: long tasks run by a model in its harness

facts.where: newsletter, methodology
facts.quote: We ran all models in their native harness when available (e.g. Claude Code for Opus 5.5, Codex for GPT 6 Astra, Antigravity for Gemini 4 Carbon, etc.). For models that don’t have a native harness, we default to OpenCode.

facts.value: sandbagged overall scores due to their safety classifiers
facts.where: newsletter, interpreting the results
facts.quote: It’s worth emphasizing that certain models like Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra have sandbagged overall scores due to their safety classifiers.
facts.note: flag: safety classifiers (cyber, biology, alignment) lower the scores of Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra; security/behaviour effect rather than capability
